transcript: Last night, I saw Family at La MaMa, an early play by Celine Song, Oscar-nominated screenwriter of Past Lives, which I loved. This was extremely different — very experimental with elements of horror and a really jarring aesthetic, think loud noises and strobe lights. It's about three half siblings in a kind of nondescript place and time but following their father's death. We learn about each of them and their respective mothers, but there's not really a plot. It's a very disturbing and fragmented piece, and it seems like the kind of thing that could’ve been devised. But even without a plot, there are clear themes and characters to interpret. I took away how violence is perpetuated over generations, as seen by how these adult siblings interact, and also the theme of inherited trauma. Generally though, it was super confusing and it won't be for everyone. It wasn't my usual taste, but I was engaged by the exercise of trying to tease it apart. With that, another program for my collection.
